nodes.name: HPNC synthesis
nodes.procedure: HPNC was fabricated by the pyrolysis of organic materials. Typically, 2.136 g Zn(NO3)2·6H2O and 1.308 g 2,6-diaminopyridine (DAP) were added into 9 g silica colloid solution (Ludox HS40, 40% in water, Sigma-Aldrich). After drying at 60°C for 24 h, the obtained composites were ball-milled at 200 rpm for 4 h. Then the resulting powder was calcined at 1020°C for 2 h with a ramping rate of 5°C min−1 under flowing nitrogen (0.6 L min−1). The pyrolyzed sample was etched with 10 wt% HF solution (It is worthy to point out that, this step should be conducted in fume hood with extreme caution and appropriate protection due to the high corrosivity and toxicity of 10 wt% HF solution.) to remove the silica templates, followed by centrifuging and washing with water several times. After drying at 60°C for 24 h, the black powder named HPNC was obtained.

nodes.name: Fe-HPNC CVD
nodes.procedure: Chemical vapor deposition (CVD) was employed for the synthesis of Fe-HPNC. Specifically, a certain amount (100, 200, 400 mg) of anhydrous FeCl3 was placed in a porcelain boat in a tube upstream of the nitrogen flow while 100 mg HPNC was evenly placed in another porcelain boat downstream of the nitrogen flow. The gap between two boats was kept 1 cm and the nitrogen flow rate was kept 0.3 L min−1. Then the temperature of the tube furnace was risen to a variety of target values (700, 800, 900 °C) with a ramping rate of 5°C min−1 and held for 3 h. After cooling down to room temperature naturally, the desired Fe-HPNC was obtained.

nodes.name: Co3O4 hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: Co3O4 nanoparticles were prepared by a facile hydrothermal reaction. Typically, 127 mg Co2(AC)2·4H2O was dissolved in 40 ml water. Then the solution was stirred at 60°C in oil bath, during which 1 ml NH3·H2O (25 wt%) was added dropwise, and kept stirring for 2 h. After that, the homogeneous mixture was transferred to a 50 ml Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and kept at 150°C for 3 h. After cooling down to room temperature, the dark brown mixture was centrifuged and washed with water several times, then freeze dried, and the fine Co3O4 powder was obtained.

nodes.name: Fe-HPNC/Co3O4 hybridization
nodes.procedure: A certain amount (30, 60, 90 mg) of Fe-HPNC and 30 mg Co3O4 were dispersed in 40 ml water. The resulting dispersion was subjected to an ultrasonic treatment for 1 h and then kept stirring for 12 h. The products were centrifuged and freeze-dried, and Fe-HPNC/Co3O4 with different ratios of Fe-HPNC to Co3O4 was obtained.

nodes.name: RuO2/C impregnation
nodes.procedure: The RuO2/C hybrids was prepared by a facile impregnation-hydrothermal oxidation of RuCl3·nH2O. Typically, 100 mg Vulcan XC-72 was dispersed in 50 ml water by ultrasonication for 1 h. Subsequently, 50 mg RuCl3·nH2O dissolved in 5 mL water was added into the XC-72 dispersion and the pH was adjusted to 10 with 0.1 M NaOH solution. Then the mixture was vigorously stirred for 12 h, followed by centrifuged and washed with water repeatedly to get the precipitate. At last, the precipitate was dried at 60°C for 12 h, followed by ramping the temperature to 200°C and dwelling for 6 h in air.

The pore size distribution (PSD) curves (Fig. S5b) confirm the hierarchically porous structure of these samples in which most pores possess a diameter of less than 20 nm and centred at a diameter of 12 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe-HPNC-800 contains 4.67 wt% N, 3.45 wt% Fe; Fe 2p peaks at 711.1 eV, 724 eV (Fe-Nₓ); N 1s shows pyridinic N (398.2 eV), Fe-Nₓ (399 eV); Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄ contains 2.71 wt% Fe, 7.89 wt% Co; Co 2p₃/₂ (779.8 eV), Co 2p₁/₂ (794.8 eV) confirming Co³⁺/Co²⁺.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The contents of N and Fe for the optimal sample, Fe-HPNC-800, are 4.67 wt% and 3.45 wt%, respectively ... Fe 2p spectra ... show two peaks at around 711.1 eV and 724 eV, attributing to the Fe-Nₓ configuration ... The XPS results of Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄ ... show that the contents of Fe and Co are 2.71 wt% and 7.89 wt%, respectively. There are two peaks in Co 2p spectra at 794.8 eV and 779.8 eV corresponding to Co 2p₃/₂ and Co 2p₁/₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄ contains 2.71 wt% Fe and 7.89 wt% Co by XPS; Fe contents 0.34-2.84 wt% for different Fe-HPNC ratios; Co content 7.29 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The contents of Fe and Co were determined by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES, Avio 200) ... The Fe contents are quantified to be 0.34, 2.04 and 2.84 wt% for Fe-HPNC-x:1 (x=1, 2, 4), respectively ... Besides, the Co content for Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄ was measured to be 7.29 wt%.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge XANES shows positively charged Fe single-atoms; FT-EXAFS shows Fe-N at 1.5 Å, Fe-C at 2.6 Å, no Fe-Fe peaks; coordination number ~2 for FeN₂ confirmed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier-transform (FT) EXAFS curve of Fe-HPNC in Fig. 3e presents a primary peak at 1.5 Å assigning to the Fe-N scattering paths while a minor peak at 2.6 Å attributing to Fe-C coordination. No obvious peaks for Fe-Fe ... an average coordination number (C_N) of about 2 was obtained for both C and N ... single Fe atoms take a FeN₂ configuration in Fe-HPNC.
